p: East Street is Barking's main pedestrianised shopping street, home to the town's market, so it's a busy, lively spot on market days. Barking station, served by the District and Hammersmith & City lines, c2c and the Overground, is at the top of the street, so it's very easy to reach.

Just south of the town centre, the ruins of Barking Abbey sit beside St Margaret's Church, where Captain James Cook was married in 1762. Barking Park, with its long boating lake, is a short walk north of the station if you fancy some green space.
